sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of jury rights in federal drug trials. It follows a lower court action that allowed a judge to set a sentence based on unproven facts.

Cotton wants the sentence reduced because the jury did not prove the drug amount.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the limits of judicial sentencing power in federal drug prosecutions. It determines whether judges can rely on unproven facts to increase prison terms. The outcome shapes the balance between prosecutorial discretion and defendant rights.
